sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球排名的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内开展合作与创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学促进所有生物生活质量这一使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: The thing about being wrong is that before you know you're wrong, it feels exactly like being right.
sentences.zh: 关于犯错，有一点是：在你意识到自己犯错之前，那种感觉和正确一模一样。

sentences.en: If we knew that we were wrong, we wouldn't be wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果我们知道自己错了，我们就不会犯错了。

sentences.en: Nobody's committing intentionally to a false belief about the world.
sentences.zh: 没有人会故意去坚持一个关于世界的错误信念。

sentences.en: If they are, they're not wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果他们真的坚持，那他们就不是错了。

sentences.en: They're deliberately lying.
sentences.zh: 他们是在蓄意撒谎。

sentences.en: Even during the construction of the original Tacoma Narrows Bridge, which was to become the third longest suspension bridge in the world, it seemed like something was wrong.
sentences.zh: 即使在最初的塔科马海峡大桥建设期间——它本将成为世界上第三长的悬索桥——似乎也有些不对劲。

sentences.en: Well, at least in hindsight, it seems like it should have felt that way, but that's not how being wrong works.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少事后看来，似乎当时就应该有这种感觉，但犯错的本质并非如此。

sentences.en: If you grew up like I did watching the Warner Brothers cartoons...
sentences.zh: 如果你像我一样，是看着华纳兄弟的动画片长大的……

sentences.en: This is Katherine Schultz, author of Being Wrong, Adventures in the Margin of Error.
sentences.zh: 这位是凯瑟琳·舒尔茨，《犯错：误差边缘的冒险》一书的作者。

sentences.en: The Sunday morning cartoon moment where the roadrunner is dashing off the cliff and the coyote is following him.
sentences.zh: 周日早晨的动画片里，那只走鹃冲下悬崖，而歪心狼紧随其后。

sentences.en: And, of course, the roadrunner can fly and the coyote can't.
sentences.zh: 当然，走鹃会飞，而歪心狼不会。

sentences.en: And there's this great moment where he's run off the cliff, but he has not yet realized that, you know, there's no solid ground underneath him.
sentences.zh: 有一个很棒的瞬间，他跑出了悬崖，但他还没有意识到，你知道的，他脚下已经没有坚实的地面了。

sentences.en: And the moment when we're wrong about something, but before we've realized it, is like that moment.
sentences.zh: 而当我们对某事犯错，但在意识到之前的那一刻，就像那个瞬间一样。

sentences.en: We think that our belief is rock solid.
sentences.zh: 我们认为自己的信念坚如磐石。

sentences.en: We think we have, you know, all of the facts in the world bolstering us.
sentences.zh: 我们认为自己掌握了世界上所有的事实来支撑我们。

sentences.en: We feel like our giant suspension bridge is not going to collapse.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得我们巨大的悬索桥不会倒塌。

sentences.en: We have not yet looked down and realized that, whoops, that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有低头看，意识到“哎呀，事实并非如此”。

sentences.en: I know this sounds crazy, but even during its construction, the deck of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge would go up and down by several feet with the slightest breeze.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很疯狂，但即使在施工期间，塔科马海峡大桥的桥面在微风中也会上下起伏好几英尺。

sentences.en: Construction workers on the span chewed on lemon wedges to stop motion sickness.
sentences.zh: 桥上的建筑工人们嚼着柠檬片来缓解晕动症。

sentences.en: But construction continued because the bridge had been designed specifically to withstand winds up to 120 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 但施工仍在继续，因为这座桥的设计初衷就是为了抵御高达每小时120英里的风速。

sentences.en: So everyone thought everything would be fine.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都认为一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: Well, almost everyone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，几乎每个人都这么认为。

sentences.en: The original Tacoma Narrows Bridge design by Clark Eldridge was pretty conventional for a suspension bridge,
sentences.zh: 克拉克·埃尔德里奇最初设计的塔科马海峡大桥对于悬索桥来说相当传统，

sentences.en: but it was later modified by Leon Moiseff to be slimmer and more elegant.
sentences.zh: 但后来被莱昂·莫伊塞夫修改得更纤细、更优雅。

sentences.en: The most notable change was the 25-foot lattice of stiffening trusses underneath the bridge on the original drawings were replaced with an 8-foot solid steel plate girder.
sentences.zh: 最显著的变化是，原图纸中桥下25英尺高的格构式加劲桁架被8英尺高的实心钢板梁所取代。

sentences.en: The new solid girder along the side in Moiseff's design made for a much lighter, slimmer, and more flexible bridge.
sentences.zh: 莫伊塞夫设计中侧面的新实心梁使桥梁变得更轻、更细、更灵活。

sentences.en: It also caught the wind like a sail, but they didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 它也像帆一样兜风，但他们当时并不知道这一点。

sentences.en: Moiseff's design was also two-thirds the price of the original Eldridge design, and that fact ultimately won the day.
sentences.zh: 莫伊塞夫的设计价格也只有埃尔德里奇原设计的的三分之二，而这一事实最终胜出。

sentences.en: Eldridge and other state engineers were said to have protested, but it didn't matter.
sentences.zh: 据说埃尔德里奇和其他州工程师曾提出抗议，但无济于事。

sentences.en: The original Tacoma Narrows Bridge opened to the public on July 1, 1940.
sentences.zh: 最初的塔科马海峡大桥于1940年7月1日向公众开放。

sentences.en: From the day it opened, it was prone to having these oscillations, these longitudinal waves of the bridge deck.
sentences.zh: 从开放的第一天起，它就容易出现这种振荡，即桥面的纵向波浪。

sentences.en: That's our master of disaster, John Marr.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的灾难大师，约翰·马尔。

sentences.en: And I write on various murders and disasters and other sundry topics.
sentences.zh: 我写过各种谋杀案、灾难和其他杂七杂八的话题。

sentences.en: He used to publish a zine called Murderer Can Be Fun about these sundry topics.
sentences.zh: 他过去曾出版过一本名为《谋杀者也很有趣》的杂志，专门讨论这些杂七杂八的话题。

sentences.en: He wrote about the Tacoma Narrows Bridge years ago.
sentences.zh: 他多年前就写过关于塔科马海峡大桥的文章。

sentences.en: The workers on the bridge had nicknamed it Galloping Gertie, and that quickly kind of became the bridge's unofficial name.
sentences.zh: 桥上的工人们给它起了个绰号叫“飞奔的格蒂”，这很快就成了这座桥非正式的名字。

sentences.en: Even light winds caused the roadway to ripple with longitudinal waves some five feet high.
sentences.zh: 即使是微风也会导致路面产生约五英尺高的涟漪状纵向波浪。

sentences.en: The state of Washington was concerned about this, but not intensely.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿州对此感到担忧，但并不强烈。

sentences.en: So they were, like, looking at various things to reduce the motion.
sentences.zh: 所以他们当时在研究各种方法来减少这种晃动。

sentences.en: They had tried some tie-down cables and installing a damper and various other things, none of which had worked.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试过一些系紧缆索、安装阻尼器以及其他各种方法，但都没有奏效。

sentences.en: But again, the roadbed seemed like it could handle the waves just fine.
sentences.zh: 但同样，路基看起来似乎完全能应付这些波浪。

sentences.en: They were very confident in the structural integrity of the bridge.
sentences.zh: 他们对桥梁的结构完整性非常有信心。

sentences.en: The bridge was as solid as the air underneath Wile E.
sentences.zh: 这座桥就像歪心狼脚下的空气一样坚固。

sentences.en: Coyote's feet.
sentences.zh: （接上句）歪心狼脚下的空气一样坚固。

sentences.en: When you watch film of the waves traveling down the bridge, it is stunning.
sentences.zh: 当你观看波浪在桥上移动的影片时，那真是令人震惊。

sentences.en: And the fact that the bridge stayed open at all really illustrates how local governments have changed since 1940.
sentences.zh: 而这座桥竟然一直保持开放，这确实说明了自1940年以来地方政府发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: That thing would never stay open today.
sentences.zh: 那东西在今天绝对不可能保持开放。

sentences.en: If you were sitting in a car on the bridge when the waves were going, the cars in front of you would bob up and then disappear completely from view.
sentences.zh: 如果你坐在桥上的车里，当波浪涌动时，你前面的车会上下颠簸，然后完全从视野中消失。

sentences.en: Almost like this real ride.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像是在坐真正的游乐设施。

sentences.en: People would actually drive specifically for the feeling of riding on this bouncing bridge.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至会专门开车去体验在这座弹跳的桥上行驶的感觉。

sentences.en: The ride ended just four months later.
sentences.zh: 这段旅程仅仅四个月后就结束了。

sentences.en: It's on a fatal day, and the wind begins to speak with a roar that no man can fail to hear.
sentences.zh: 那是一个致命的日子，风开始发出任何人都无法忽视的咆哮声。

sentences.en: It was clear early on the morning of November 7th that the gale force winds were having a greater effect on the bridge than ever before.
sentences.zh: 11月7日清晨，很明显，大风对桥梁的影响比以往任何时候都要大。

sentences.en: Previously, these sorts of waves on the bridge had been, like, fairly transitory.
sentences.zh: 以前，桥上的这类波浪通常是相当短暂的。

sentences.en: You know, it could bounce up for a couple minutes, but this was just going on and on, so they thought this could be problematical.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它可能会弹跳几分钟，但这次却持续不断，所以他们认为这可能会是个问题。

sentences.en: Although they had seen, actually, deeper waves on the bridge.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们实际上已经见过桥上更深的波浪。

sentences.en: But then the movement changed.
sentences.zh: 但随后运动方式改变了。

sentences.en: Things, you know, just got worse.
sentences.zh: 事情，你知道的，变得更糟了。

sentences.en: The bridge began to twist violently along the center line.
sentences.zh: 桥梁开始沿着中心线剧烈扭曲。

sentences.en: And that became, like, extremely violent.
sentences.zh: 那变得极其剧烈。

sentences.en: One end of the bridge deck was up at a 45-degree angle.
sentences.zh: 桥面的一端向上倾斜到了45度角。

sentences.en: In a 40-mile-an-hour gale, the center span weaves like a ribbon in a swinging twist that you wouldn't believe possible
sentences.zh: 在每小时40英里的狂风中，中心跨度像丝带一样在摆动中扭曲，你简直无法相信这是可能的，

sentences.en: as the bridge gyrates like a nightmare high above the river, twisting, turning, curling.
sentences.zh: 当桥梁像噩梦一样在河面上方高处旋转、扭动、翻转、卷曲时。

sentences.en: By this time, everyone had gotten off.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，所有人都已经撤离了。

sentences.en: The blunt, solid edge of the bridge disrupted the flow of the strong wind, causing one part to twist up while the other section twisted down.
sentences.zh: 桥梁钝而坚实的边缘扰乱了强风的流动，导致一部分向上扭曲，而另一部分向下扭曲。

sentences.en: And it continued this torsional back and forth for over an hour, so there was plenty of time for spectators to come watch,
sentences.zh: 这种扭转往复持续了一个多小时，所以有足够的时间让观众前来观看，

sentences.en: including the bridge's original designer, Clark Eldridge.
sentences.zh: 包括这座桥最初的设计师克拉克·埃尔德里奇。

sentences.en: A local camera store owner named Barney Elliott arrived on the scene and took the now-famous color film of the bridge's relentless gyrations.
sentences.zh: 当地一家照相馆的老板巴尼·埃利奥特赶到现场，拍摄了那段如今著名的、关于大桥持续扭转的彩色影片。

sentences.en: No structure of steel and concrete can stand such a strain.
sentences.zh: 没有任何钢筋混凝土结构能承受这样的压力。

sentences.en: Steel girders buckle, and giant cables snap like CUNY threads.
sentences.zh: 钢梁弯曲，巨大的缆索像细线一样崩断。

sentences.en: There it goes!
sentences.zh: 它倒了！

sentences.en: Engineers are divided as to the cause of the disaster.
sentences.zh: 工程师们对灾难的原因各执一词。

sentences.en: Some claim it was the use of solid girders.
sentences.zh: 有人声称是因为使用了实心梁。

sentences.en: Others differ.
sentences.zh: 其他人则有不同看法。

sentences.en: But whatever the reason, Tacoma will rebuild.
sentences.zh: 但无论原因如何，塔科马都会重建。

sentences.en: This time a bridge that will not provide a super thrill in the news.
sentences.zh: 这一次，这座桥将不会再成为新闻中那种令人心惊肉跳的奇观。

sentences.en: Before the collapse, bridge aerodynamics and structural failure due to torsion had scarcely been considered.
sentences.zh: 在倒塌之前，桥梁空气动力学和因扭转导致的结构失效几乎从未被考虑过。

sentences.en: Or maybe those lessons had been lost in the rapid evolution of more and more slender and longer bridges.
sentences.zh: 或者也许那些教训在桥梁变得越来越细长、跨度越来越大的快速演变中被遗忘了。

sentences.en: But the failure caused the study of bridge aerodynamics to take off,
sentences.zh: 但这次失败促使桥梁空气动力学的研究突飞猛进，

sentences.en: and any bridges that were on the drawing board in 1940 were redesigned with more conservative, deep-open-trust deck structures.
sentences.zh: 1940年时所有在绘图板上的桥梁设计都被重新设计，采用了更保守、深开敞式的桁架结构。

sentences.en: The lead designer, Leon Moiseff, and his solid steel I-beams received most of the blame for the disaster.
sentences.zh: 首席设计师莱昂·莫伊塞夫及其设计的实心工字钢梁受到了此次灾难的大部分指责。

sentences.en: He never designed another bridge again.
sentences.zh: 他再也没有设计过另一座桥梁。

sentences.en: Due in no small part to the fact that he died three years later.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为他在三年后就去世了。

sentences.en: No one was killed on the bridge.
sentences.zh: 没有人在这座桥上丧生。

sentences.en: A few people were very lucky to get away with their lives because,
sentences.zh: 有几个人非常幸运地保住了性命，因为，

sentences.en: I just imagine you're on this bridge and it's twisting at a 45-degree angle and you're trying to walk off in a fairly stiff wind.
sentences.zh: 我只是想象一下，你在这座桥上，它正以45度角扭曲，而你正试图在相当大的风中走下去。

sentences.en: The only casualty was a dog.
sentences.zh: 唯一的伤亡是一只狗。

sentences.en: A local newspaper man named Leonard Coatsworth drove his car just past the East Tower when the twisting started.
sentences.zh: 当地一位名叫伦纳德·科茨沃斯的报社记者在扭转开始时，刚把车开过东塔。

sentences.en: It got bouncing so hard he couldn't control his car anymore.
sentences.zh: 车子颠簸得太厉害，他再也无法控制自己的车了。

sentences.en: The tilting bridge threw his car into the side curb.
sentences.zh: 倾斜的桥面把他的车甩到了路边的路缘石上。

sentences.en: And he had his daughter's dog, Cocker Spaniel, named Tubby with him.
sentences.zh: 他带着他女儿的狗，一只名叫塔比的可卡犬。

sentences.en: Coatsworth gets out of his wrecked vehicle and gets thrown face down on the curb.
sentences.zh: 科茨沃斯从撞毁的车里爬出来，脸朝下摔在路缘石上。

sentences.en: The dog's completely freaked out.
sentences.zh: 那只狗完全吓坏了。

sentences.en: He couldn't get the dog out.
sentences.zh: 他没能把狗救出来。

sentences.en: He hears the concrete cracking beneath him.
sentences.zh: 他听见身下的混凝土在开裂。

sentences.en: And he barely makes it to safety.
sentences.zh: 他勉强逃到了安全地带。

sentences.en: An engineering professor studying the bridge named Farkarsen ventured out to get Tubby right when the bridge was about to fall into the sound.
sentences.zh: 一位研究该桥的工程学教授法卡森在桥即将坠入海峡时，冒险出去救塔比。

sentences.en: But when he reached into the car, Tubby bit him.
sentences.zh: 但当他伸手进车里时，塔比咬了他。

sentences.en: The dog was just too freaked out to leave the vehicle.
sentences.zh: 那只狗被吓坏了，不肯离开车子。

sentences.en: There's amazing film of Farkarsen stumbling back as best he could, sticking to that middle yellow line as the bridge rocked wildly along its center axis.
sentences.zh: 有一段令人惊叹的影片，法卡森尽其所能踉跄着往回走，紧贴着中间的黄线，而桥梁正沿着中心轴剧烈摇晃。

sentences.en: So, Tubby was the only casualty and, you know, the poor guy always said, you know, God, I have to tell my daughter this.
sentences.zh: 所以，塔比是唯一的伤亡者，你知道的，那个可怜的人总是说，天哪，我该怎么告诉我的女儿。

sentences.en: Coatsworth was quoted immediately after the collapse, saying,
sentences.zh: 科茨沃斯在倒塌后立即被引用说：

sentences.en: With real tragedy, disaster, and blasted dreams all around me.
sentences.zh: “周围全是真正的悲剧、灾难和破碎的梦想。”

sentences.en: I believe that right at this minute, what appalls me most is that within a few hours, I must tell my daughter that her dog is dead when I might have saved him.
sentences.zh: “我相信就在这一刻，最让我震惊的是，几个小时内，我就必须告诉女儿她的狗死了，而我本可以救它的。”

sentences.en: This next bit is a completely unrelated addendum that will serve as a valuable life lesson to any 99% Invisible fan.
sentences.zh: 接下来的这段是一个完全无关的附录，它将为任何《99%隐形》的粉丝提供一个宝贵的人生教训。

sentences.en: Here's John Marr again.
sentences.zh: 再次请出约翰·马尔。

sentences.en: Several years ago, I went to the Portland Zine Symposium to do a seminar on research-based zines.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我去参加波特兰杂志研讨会，举办了一个关于研究型杂志的研讨会。

sentences.en: Research-based zines, like research-based blogs or podcasts, have always been a bit in the minority.
sentences.zh: 研究型杂志，就像研究型博客或播客一样，一直都是少数派。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: And it was held in this building called the Michael Smith Memorial Student Union Building on the Portland State University campus.
sentences.zh: 它是在波特兰州立大学校园里的一栋名为迈克尔·史密斯纪念学生会大楼里举行的。

sentences.en: The very first thing I did, I got up in front of the class and said,
sentences.zh: 我做的第一件事，就是站在班级前面说：

sentences.en: Okay, this panel is being held in the Michael Smith Memorial Student Union Building.
sentences.zh: “好吧，这个小组讨论是在迈克尔·史密斯纪念学生会大楼举行的。”

sentences.en: Does anyone know who Michael Smith was?
sentences.zh: “有人知道迈克尔·史密斯是谁吗？”

sentences.en: No one did.
sentences.zh: 没人知道。

sentences.en: Michael Smith was the captain of the Portland State University College Bowl team.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·史密斯是波特兰州立大学大学碗队的队长。

sentences.en: The College Bowl was a televised trivia competition matching teams from various universities throughout the country.
sentences.zh: 大学碗是一项电视转播的知识竞赛，汇集了全国各大学的队伍。

sentences.en: And he led Portland State University to the championship, which is just an incredible accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 他带领波特兰州立大学获得了冠军，这真是一个不可思议的成就。

sentences.en: They're beating out schools like Harvard and Yale.
sentences.zh: 他们击败了哈佛和耶鲁这样的学校。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is Portland State.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是波特兰州立大学。

sentences.en: This is a state school.
sentences.zh: 这是一所州立学校。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not the type of school that you expect to win something like this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是你期望能赢得这种比赛的学校类型。

sentences.en: I'm sure the Ivy League people were horribly embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定常春藤盟校的人当时一定尴尬极了。

sentences.en: And it was quite a big deal at the time.
sentences.zh: 这在当时确实是一件大事。

sentences.en: He also was suffering from cystic fibrosis, and he would die three years after this.
sentences.zh: 他还患有囊性纤维化，三年后就去世了。

sentences.en: So, everyone agreed this was a good story.
sentences.zh: 所以，大家都同意这是一个好故事。

sentences.en: They asked me, how'd you find out about this?
sentences.zh: 他们问我，你是怎么发现这个的？

sentences.en: There's a plaque in front of the building.
sentences.zh: 大楼前有一块牌匾。

sentences.en: My slogan is, always read the plaque.
sentences.zh: 我的座右铭是：永远阅读牌匾。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由我，罗曼·马尔斯制作。

sentences.en: A special thanks to John Marr of Murder Can Be Fun and Alan Bellows of the website Damn Interesting.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢《谋杀者也很有趣》的约翰·马尔和网站《该死有趣》的艾伦·贝洛斯。

sentences.en: We are a project of KALW 91.7 Local Public Radio in San Francisco and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山KALW 91.7地方公共广播电台和旧金山美国建筑师协会的一个项目。

sentences.en: Support for 99% Invisible is provided in part by Tiny Letter, email for people with something to say.
sentences.zh: 《99%隐形》的部分支持由Tiny Letter提供，这是为有话要说的人准备的电子邮件服务。

sentences.en: My boy Maslow always has something to say.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子马斯洛总是有话要说。

sentences.en: What do you have to say, Maslow?
sentences.zh: 你想说什么，马斯洛？

sentences.en: My favorite thing to talk about is robots and Iron Man suits and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢谈论的是机器人、钢铁侠套装之类的东西。

sentences.en: Robots and Iron Man suits.
sentences.zh: 机器人和钢铁侠套装。

sentences.en: I would subscribe to that newsletter.
sentences.zh: 我会订阅那个通讯。

sentences.en: It's free, easy, minimal, powerful, the simplest way to write an email newsletter.
sentences.zh: 它免费、简单、极简、强大，是撰写电子邮件通讯最简单的方式。

sentences.en: Online at tinyletter.com
sentences.zh: 在线访问 tinyletter.com

sentences.en: This program is distributed by PRX, the public radio exchange, making public radio more public.
sentences.zh: 本节目由公共广播交流平台PRX发行，让公共广播更加大众化。

sentences.en: Find out more at prx.org
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问 prx.org

sentences.en: And while I'm talking about PRX, I have to tell you about another podcast they produce called How Sound by the genius Rob Rosenthal.
sentences.zh: 在谈论PRX的同时，我必须向你们介绍他们制作的另一个播客，由天才罗伯·罗森塔尔主持的《How Sound》。

sentences.en: If you're a person who loves radio and is also the type of person who listens to the director's commentary on DVDs, then How Sound is the show for you.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个热爱广播的人，同时也是那种会听DVD导演评论的人，那么《How Sound》就是为你准备的节目。

sentences.en: Check it out at howsound.org
sentences.zh: 请访问 howsound.org 查看。

sentences.en: My man Sam Greenspan took off for a while to launch the TED Radio Hour at NPR.
sentences.zh: 我的伙计萨姆·格林斯潘暂时离开了，去 NPR 创办了《TED 广播时间》节目。

sentences.en: But he'll be back.
sentences.zh: 但他会回来的。

sentences.en: You'll be back, Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 你会回来的，格林斯潘。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并点赞这个节目。

sentences.en: I would like it if you would like us.
sentences.zh: 如果你能点赞我们，我会很高兴的。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars, but you can always catch up with us online at 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 我会在 Roman Mars 的账号发推文，但你随时可以在 99% Invisible 的网站上关注我们的动态。

sentences.en: .org
sentences.zh: .org
